subject: Math
prompt: The expression $6x^{3} + 19x^{2} + 2x - 3$ can be written as $(ax + b)(2x^{2} + cx + 3)$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are integer constants. Which of the following is the value of $a + c$?
explanation: Expanding $(ax + b)(2x^2 + cx + 3)$ gives $2ax^3 + acx^2 + 3ax + 2bx^2 + bcx + 3b = 2ax^3 + (ac + 2b)x^2 + (3a + bc)x + 3b$. Comparing with $6x^3 + 19x^2 + 2x - 3$: from $2a = 6$, we get $a = 3$; from $3b = -3$, we get $b = -1$. Substituting into $ac + 2b = 19$ gives $3c - 2 = 19$, so $c = 7$. Checking: $3a + bc = 9 + (-1)(7) = 2$. Therefore $a + c = 3 + 7 = 10$.
